It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was prefectural shrine. {{nihongo|'''Takahashi Shrine'''|高椅神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ckb|پارێزگای شیمۆسا|cs|Provincie Šimósa|de|Provinz Shimousa|es|Provincia de Shimōsa|fa|ولایت شیموسا|fr|Province de Shimōsa|gl|Provincia de Shimōsa|hak|Shimōsa-koet|id|Provinsi Shimousa|it|Shimōsa|ja|下総国|ko|시모사국|lt|Šimosos žemė|nl|Shimosa (provincie)|pt|Província de Shimōsa|ru|Симоса (провинция)|simple|Shimōsa Province|sk|Šimósa|sr|Провинција Шимоса|tr|Shimōsa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сімоса|zh|下總國|zh_min_nan|Simôsa-kok|zh_yue|下總國|qid=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}}.

It is the oldest shrine whose main deity is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto}}, revered as the "ancestral deity of {{ill|Cuisine|ar|مطبخ (أسلوب)|as|ৰন্ধনশৈলী|atj|Tcipakwan|ba|Аш-һыу (традициялар)|be|Кухня|bg|Кухня|bh|पकवान (इस्टाइल)|bn|রন্ধনশৈলী|br|Keginerezh|ca|Cuina|ckb|دەستاو|cs|Kuchyně (způsob přípravy jídla)|cv|Кухня (традици)|da|Kogekunst|el|Κουζίνα|eo|Kuirarto|es|Cocina (tradiciones)|eu|Sukaldaritza|fa|روش آشپزی|fi|Ruokakulttuuri|fr|Cuisine|gl|Arte culinaria|he|סגנון בישול|hi|पाकशैली|hr|Kulinarstvo|hy|Խոհանոց (ավանդույթներ)|id|Hidangan|ig|Cuisine|io|Koquajaro|is|Matarhefð|isv|Kuhnja|it|Cucina (attività)|ja|料理|jv|Olahan|knc|Kәmbube|ko|요리|lad|Kuzina|lfn|Cosini|lt|Pasaulio virtuvės|mr|पाककला|ms|Masakan|nap|Cucina|new|नसापहः|nl|Keuken (kookwijze)|nn|Kokekunst|pa|ਪਕਵਾਨ|pcd|Tchuisinne|pt|Culinária|ro|Cuisine|ru|Кухня (традиции)|sc|Coghina|sh|Kulinarstvo|si|සූපවේදය|simple|Cuisine|sk|Kuchárske umenie|sq|Kuzhinieria|sr|Кулинарство|sv|Matkultur|sw|Kupika|th|การครัว|tr|Mutfak (kültür)|tt|Аш-су (традицияләр)|uk|Кухня|uz|Oshxona (anʼanalar)|vi|Ẩm thực|war|Panluto|zh|菜系|zh_min_nan|Liāu-lí|zh_yue|菜系|qid=Q1778821}}." ==History==
According to shrine tradition, in {{ill|AD 111|ab|111|af|111|als|111|am|111 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|111|ar|111|ary|111|ast|111|avk|111|az|111|azb|۱۱۱ (میلادی)|be|111|be_x_old|111|bg|111|bn|১১১|bpy|মারি ১১১|br|111|bs|111.|ca|111|cdo|111 nièng|ceb|111|ckb|١١١|crh|111|cs|111|cv|111|cy|111|da|111|de|111|el|111|eml|111|eo|111|es|111|et|111|eu|111|fa|۱۱۱ (میلادی)|fi|111|fo|111|fr|111|fy|111|ga|111|gan|111年|gd|111|gl|111|he|111|ht|111 (almanak jilyen)|hu|111|hy|111|ia|111|id|111|io|111|is|111|it|111|ja|111年|jv|111|ka|111|kk|111 жыл|ko|111년|la|111|lb|111|lij|111|lmo|111|lt|111 m.|map_bms|111|mdf|111|mg|111|mhr|111|min|111|mk|111|mr|इ.स. १११|mrj|111 и|ms|111|mzn|۱۱۱ (میلادی)|nap|111|nds|111|nds_nl|111|new|सन् १११|nl|111|nn|111|no|111|nso|111|oc|111|or|୧୧୧|os|111-æм аз|pa|111|pl|111|pnb|111|pt|111|qu|111|ro|111|ru|111 год|rue|111|sa|१११|sah|111|sd|111ع|sh|111.|si|111|sk|111|sl|111|sq|111|sr|111|srn|111|su|111|sv|111|sw|111|tg|Соли 111|th|พ.ศ. 654|tk|111|tl|111|tly|111|tr|111|tt|111 ел|uk|111|ur|111ء|uz|111|vec|111|vi|111|war|111|wuu|111年|xmf|111|zh|111年|zh_classical|一一一年|zh_min_nan|111 nî|zh_yue|111年|qid=Q30640}} (Keikō 41), when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|arz|ياماتو تاكيرو|be|Ямата Такэру|de|Yamatotakeru|es|Yamato Takeru|fa|یاماتو تاکه‌رو|fr|Yamato Takeru|hu|Jamatotakeru|id|Yamato Takeru|it|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|ko|야마토타케루|pt|Yamato Takeru|ru|Ямато Такэру|sh|Yamato Takeru|simple|Yamato Takeru|sq|Jamato Takeru|sr|Јамато Такеру|sv|Yamato Takeru|tr|Yamato Takeru|uk|Ямато Такеру|ur|یاماتو تاکیرو|vi|Yamato Takeru|zh|日本武尊|zh_min_nan|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258}} campaigned eastward, he invited Kunitokotachi-no-Mikoto, Amakagami-no-Mikoto, and Amayorozu-no-Mikoto here and prayed for victory. When Emperor Keikō later inspected the campaign sites, Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kashiwade no Omi}} line, was old and with imperial permission remained here. Since then, parishioners do not eat carp, do not use vessels painted with carp, and do not raise {{ill|Koinobori|ar|كوينوبوري|ast|Koinobori|cs|Koinobori|de|Koinobori|eo|Koi Nobori|es|Koinobori|fa|کوینوبوری|fr|Koi nobori|id|Koinobori|it|Koinobori|ja|こいのぼり|jv|Koinobori|ko|고이노보리|nl|Koinobori|pl|Koi-nobori|pt|Koinobori|ro|Koinobori|ru|Коинобори|sco|Koinobori|tr|Koinobori|vi|Koinobori|zh|鯉魚旗|qid=Q779745}} in May. From this comes the alternate name '''Carp Myōjin'''.

In the medieval period it was protected by the {{ill|Yūki clan|de|Yūki (Klan)|fr|Clan Yūki|it|Clan Yūki|ja|結城氏|ko|유키씨|pt|Clã Yūki-Matsudaira|ru|Юки (род)|uk|Рід Юкі|qid=Q2975399}} of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ckb|پارێزگای شیمۆسا|cs|Provincie Šimósa|de|Provinz Shimousa|es|Provincia de Shimōsa|fa|ولایت شیموسا|fr|Province de Shimōsa|gl|Provincia de Shimōsa|hak|Shimōsa-koet|id|Provinsi Shimousa|it|Shimōsa|ja|下総国|ko|시모사국|lt|Šimosos žemė|nl|Shimosa (provincie)|pt|Província de Shimōsa|ru|Симоса (провинция)|simple|Shimōsa Province|sk|Šimósa|sr|Провинција Шимоса|tr|Shimōsa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сімоса|zh|下總國|zh_min_nan|Simôsa-kok|zh_yue|下總國|qid=Q1053695}}. More than 20 documents remain, including donation letters, prayers, and practice records from castle lords {{ill|Yūki Masaasahi|ja|結城政朝|qid=Q11606587}}, {{ill|Yūki Masanao|ja|結城政直|qid=Q11606589}}, {{ill|Yūki Masakatsu|el|Γιούκι Μασακάτσου|fr|Yūki Masakatsu|it|Yūki Masakatsu|ja|結城政勝|pt|Yūki Masakatsu|zh|结城政胜|qid=Q8062739}}, {{ill|Yūki Harutomo|fr|Yūki Harutomo|it|Yūki Harutomo|ja|結城晴朝|pt|Yūki Harutomo|zh|結城晴朝|qid=Q8062736}}, and {{ill|Yūki Hideyasu|arz|يوكى هيدياسو|eo|Yuki Hideyasu|fa|یوکی هیده‌یاسو|fr|Yūki Hideyasu|it|Yūki Hideyasu|ja|結城秀康|ko|유키 히데야스|pt|Yūki Hideyasu|ru|Юки Хидэясу|uk|Юкі Хідеясу|zh|結城秀康|qid=Q1130929}}. Even after Hideyasu was transferred to Echizen Fukui, ceremonial proxy visits were maintained generation after generation until the Meiji Restoration.

== Oyama City designated intangible cultural property ==

== Chinowa crossing ==
The chinowa ring at Takahashi Shrine has a rare square shape, about 2 m per side, not circular. The reason is unknown. It is made with one-sided reed as core, wrapped in makomo and bound with cogon-grass rope<ref>Yomiuri Shimbun Tochigi edition, August 3, 2017, p.29.</ref>.
